what: The owner's measured key section: a natural of the middle of a grand keyboard, its keystick, covering, key front, glued blocks, thinned tail and its felt, chamfer, front mortise and capstan's place as he measured them on his keys, on the key frame he measured, its rails placed under the key by the rule a frame is built to, regulated on arrival. Not weighed: nobody has weighed one of these keys whole, so the key has no mass until the bench's user weighs one, and every reading that needs its mass is refused until then: front weight, down and up weight, balance and friction weight, Stanwood's key friction weight and the band. Key height, dip, the key weight ratio, the key friction weight zeroed on the frame and the faults read no mass, and are read. Where the key stands along its balance pin is not measured: its key front is assumed 258 mm in front of the pin, and its tail follows from its measured length.
instruments: natural keys from a grand piano keyboard

key_kind.why: A natural of the middle of the keyboard: it stands on the row of pins in front, which is the row the owner's frame was measured on.

key_mass.why: Nobody has weighed one of these keys. An outline draws a key and never weighs it, and another key's mass on these arms would describe no key, so the key has no mass until it is weighed whole on the bench, as a key that arrives leaded is weighed: its mass on a scale, and its front weight on Stanwood's jig with how far back from the covering's lip the weight was centered. What would replace this: one of these keys weighed so, the three numbers typed in the bench's weighing; the height of its center of mass, which no scale gives, is then estimated from the drawn section's area centroid.

arrival.why: Built as a technician hands over a frame: regulated before it is weighed. The papers on both punchings are those the regulation solve lays from the drawer to the targets below, so no paper is a starting value of its own.

values.why: Not measured: where the key front stands in front of the balance pin, which the owner's measurement of the distance from the center of the balance hole to the key front, or to the covering's lip, would replace. Assumed 13 mm ahead of Thorin's 245 mm key arm (Thorin 2013, Table 2.1). Key height and dip are read here, and every touchweight through the measuring point, 13 mm behind the covering's lip 2 mm further forward, at 247 mm: with the capstan measured 122 mm behind the pin, a key weight ratio of 0.494, a hundredth under the 0.50 to 0.60 published for a natural.

values.rule: The key's measured overall length, 500 mm from its end to the covering's lip (key-section.json, key_length_overall), laid back from the lip at 258 + 2 = 260 mm: 260 - 500 = -240 mm.
values.why: The measured length placed on the assumed key front, so it rests on that assumption and moves with it until the balance pin's place along the key is measured.

Assumed: 1.3 mm of bushing cloth on each straight wall of the mortise, as in the balance mortise; the mortise's assumed 6.0 mm cutter is the front rail pin's 3.4 mm and this cloth on each side. Not measured.

Assumed: the cloth runs 3.0 mm up the mortise's walls from the groove's floor, as far as the groove is deep; the mortise is bushed in its lower part only (key-section.json, front_mortise_construction). Not measured.

Assumed: the cloth is glued 5.0 mm flat on the groove's floor from the mortise's wall, a strip that stops short of the key's side, 8.0 mm from the wall, as in the owner's photograph (key-section.json, front_mortise_construction). Not measured.
Drawn centered on the balance pin: where the key button sits along the key is not measured (key-section.json, still_to_measure). Drawn and read by nothing else.

Assumed: twice the key button's 6.0 mm height, 12.0 mm, the proportion of the owner's sketch of a key button, its ends rounded from its flat top down to the key (balance-mortise.json, construction). Not measured.

values.rule: The balance pin's 3.4 mm diameter (key-frame-sections.json, balance_pin_diameter) plus the bushing's two 1.3 mm thicknesses: 6.0 mm, the slot's width.
values.why: Derived from the assumed bushing, so that the key has the least side play on its pin. Not measured.

Assumed: a slot three times the balance pin's 3.4 mm diameter long (key-frame-sections.json, balance_pin_diameter), 10.2 mm, the proportion of the owner's sketch, less the 6.0 mm cutter: 4.2 mm. It leaves the pin 3.4 mm either side, more than the key's tilt moves it at the key button's top. Not measured.
Assumed: about a tenth of the keystick's height, the proportion of the owner's sketch, where the balance hole is drilled. Not measured.

values.rule: Fitted to the pin: the balance pin's 3.4 mm diameter (key-frame-sections.json, balance_pin_diameter).
values.why: The owner: the balance hole at the cavity's floor is fitted to the pin, which holds the key fore and aft. Not measured.
Assumed: 1.3 mm of bushing cloth on each long side of the slot. Not measured.
Assumed: half the key button's 6.0 mm height, 3.0 mm, the proportion of the owner's sketch; the slot is bushed in its upper part only (balance-mortise.json, construction). Not measured.
Assumed: twice the bushing's 1.3 mm thickness, 2.6 mm, the owner's default; the side hole is taller than the cloth, which passes through it easily (balance-mortise.json, construction). Not measured.

values.rule: Where the measured thinned tail ends on this key, the tail beginning right behind the block as measured: the key's end at -240 mm plus the tail's 20 mm (key-section.json, tail_length) = -220 mm.
values.why: Derived, not measured: the block's own place along the key is not measured. Placed from the balance pin, as the action places it, so a key lengthened at the back keeps it. It bounds how far back the capstan and the thinned tail may reach.

The owner's keys have a clearance cut in their top between the capstan and the back check block, so that the wippen rail cannot rub them, the key coming back to its full height behind it. Its two ends and its depth are not measured (key-section.json, still_to_measure): until they are, the top is drawn at its full height, and the drawn section, whose centroid estimates the height of a weighed key's center of mass, keeps the wood the clearance takes out. Nothing touches the top there.
Assumed: the key's width across the keyboard, which the solid view extrudes it by, the mortises are milled no wider than and the front mortise's groove runs across; no reading depends on it.
Where the bench first sets the capstan's head above the keystick, in proportion with the owner's close photograph of a capstan on a grand key. A regulating screw, turned continuously from here.
The threaded shaft, scaled from the owner's close photograph of a capstan on a grand key, not measured with callipers. The thread itself is not drawn.

The head, small against the shaft, with a cross hole for the regulating tool, scaled from the owner's photograph. Its flat top is what bears on the wippen's heel, and where the key weight ratio's load is centered.
The head's cylindrical part, scaled from the owner's photograph.
The short cove flaring the shaft into the head, scaled from the owner's photograph.
The threaded shaft below the cove, part of it buried in the key; scaled from the owner's photograph.
The shaft's pointed tip, scaled from the owner's photograph.
The head's top is flat, as the owner's photograph shows it: it bears on the wippen's heel with its flat, and the key weight ratio's load is centered on it.

Not measured, but not free: a correctly set key is level at the bottom of its travel and slightly nose-up when released, which puts the balance bearing above the back bearing by the dip times the back arm over the key front's arm (10.2 x 212 / 258 = 8.4 mm, where the key bears on the cloth's back edge, 212 mm behind the pin), less the 1.6 mm the chamfer has risen there. Each rail is placed so that the targets are met with a positive stack of real paper on it.

Not measured: placed so that the dip target is met with a positive stack of real paper on the front punching, the front punching coming up to the height of the balance punching with the key level at the bottom of its travel.
Not measured: with its cloth, it sets the key's rest attitude together with the balance bearing, by the relation stated for the balance rail.

Assumed, and deliberately thin, so that regulating to the targets leaves positive paper under the balance punching: a felt thicker than the whole stack the regulation calls for is a wrong washer, which the regulation refuses with its shortfall.
Assumed, and deliberately thin, so that regulating to the dip target leaves positive paper on the front punching.
Assumed: the back rail cloth's thickness has not been measured (key-frame-sections.json, still_to_measure).

Assumed: a shape, not a setting. The cloth's two top edges are rounded so that where the key bears on an edge is essentially the end of the cloth's face, and still a real curve. The contact reads the arcs as drawn; the dip moves by less than 5 µm when the radius is doubled.

values.rule: Under the key's front mortise: the key front's 258 mm less the mortise's 33 mm from it.
values.why: Placed under this key by the rule a frame is built to, then kept as recorded: a frame does not follow a key edited afterwards, and the faults name the drift.

values.rule: Set in from the key's end at -240 mm by the 40 mm of back_rail.from_the_tail: -240 + 40 = -200 mm.
values.why: Placed under this key by the rule a frame is built to, then kept as recorded.
Assumed: the crown's height above its shoulder has not been measured (key-frame-sections.json, still_to_measure). Drawn, and read by nothing else.

Assumed: the regulated balance punching's 2.2 mm, its felt and the papers the regulation lays, the keystick's 24.5 mm, the key button's 6.0 mm, and 2.5 mm above it, 35.2 mm. The owner states that the pin stands above the key button at rest (balance-mortise.json, construction); how far is the proportion of his sketch, not measured. It is drawn, and it is where the key leaves its pin, past which a pull or the key's stops take it off its frame.
The front rail is a plain block, its punchings bearing on its top.
Assumed, to be measured: a back rail 24 mm along the key, where the tail bears on its cloth (key-frame-sections.json, still_to_measure).
The back rail is a plain block, its cloth along its whole top.
No pin stands in the back rail: the key's tail rests on its cloth.

values.rule: No pin stands in the back rail, so none stands above it.
values.why: A rail section holds a pin's height whether or not the rail has a pin.

values.rule: No punching sits on the back rail: its cloth does.
values.why: A rail section holds a punching's size whether or not the rail has one.

values.rule: No punching sits on the back rail, so none is pierced.
values.why: A rail section holds a punching's hole whether or not the rail has one.

values.rule: Naturals and sharps meet the back rail's cloth at one place: the rail has one row.
values.why: A rail section holds the offset between its two rows of pins whether or not it has two.

Of the order of the key friction weight the trade measures on a well-centered key, a starting value to be replaced by a measurement, and the one value the non-confusion tests scale. Set as the torque 6 g overcome at the measuring point with the key level, an assumption and not a reading: Stanwood's protocol, run on the key resting nose-up, reads these bushings a few tenths of a gram heavier.
Close to, not equal to, the published Steinway New York key height of 65.88 mm.
Close to the published key dips: 10.16 mm Steinway New York, 9.9 to 10.6 mm Hamburg, 10.1 to 10.3 mm Kawai.

values.rule: Nothing stands on the measuring point.
values.why: The bench starts with the key at rest under no weight; a weight is what an experiment puts on it.
